blocks.text: The water (hydrological) cycle is the continuous movement of water between the abiotic components (air, soil and sea) and the biotic components.

items: Evaporation: the sun powers the cycle, heating surface water so that it evaporates. About 86% of global evaporation is from the oceans; for Pakistan the Arabian Sea is the main source of vapour that travels inland.
Condensation: rising vapour loses heat; when the air is cold enough it turns back into droplets or ice crystals, which cling to dust particles to form clouds.
Precipitation: when droplets become too heavy they fall as rain, snow or sleet (rain mixed with snow or hail).

Infiltration and runoff: on land, water either seeps into the soil (percolation) down to the water table and is stored as groundwater, or flows over the surface when the soil can take no more, into streams, rivers and the oceans.

blocks.alt: The sun heats the Arabian Sea; an arrow shows evaporation rising to clouds (condensation). Rain falls on land (precipitation). Water runs off the land into rivers and the sea (surface runoff) or sinks into the ground (infiltration) to the groundwater. A tree releases water by transpiration, and a note lists how animals take in and return water.

blocks.long_description: In the abiotic loop the sun heats surface water, which evaporates (about 86% of global evaporation is from the oceans; for Pakistan the Arabian Sea is the main source). Rising vapour cools and condenses on dust into clouds, and when droplets grow heavy they fall as rain, snow or sleet. On land water either infiltrates the soil to recharge groundwater or runs off over the surface into streams, rivers and the sea. In the biotic loop plants absorb water through root hairs and animals drink and eat it; water returns through transpiration from leaves, respiration, excretion and egestion, sweating and decomposition.

items: Entry: plants absorb water from the soil through root hairs and use it in photosynthesis and for support (turgor); animals drink and get water from food.

Exit: transpiration through leaf stomata is the main exit from plants; respiration produces metabolic water that is exhaled; animals lose water in urine, faeces and sweat; and decomposition of dead bodies releases water to soil and air.

blocks.title: Tidbits: the Indus and the water cycle
blocks.text: In Pakistan, whose agriculture and economy depend on the Indus river system, the water cycle is the nation's lifeline: surface runoff feeds the Indus, while infiltration recharges the aquifers used for drinking water.
